newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen firm despite new arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen firm despite new arrivals.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to hold onto recent gains and could rise slightly this week despite the arrival of fresh supplies of the commodity in Europe, coconut oil dealers said on Tuesday.
The vessels making the deliveries were carrying coconut oil from the Philippines, the dealers said.
"I expect prices to remain high because all the stocks from MV Star Sapphire delivered in Rotterdam last week were gobbled immediately by users," said one trader.
MV Star Sapphire was carrying an estimated cargo of 30,000 tonnes to 36,000 tonnes of coconut oil, traders said.
Another vessel, MV Kenwood, with a cargo of 30,000 tonnes to 38,000 tonnes of coconut oil, will arrive on Wednesday or Thursday in Rotterdam, they said.
"But the bulk of Kenwood's stocks have been bought ahead by consumers in Europe," said one trader.
Deliveries this week and in the past week from the Philippines to Rotterdam and the United States will total about 88,000 tonnes of coconut oil.
Europe and the United States have a demand of 45,000 tonnes of coconut oil each month, they said.
Traders said demand for coconut oil is rising due to preparations for the Christmas season.
A $10 increase for coconut oil prices for nearby months this week would be likely, traders said.
Sellers pegged coconut oil on its way to Rotterdam at $830 a tonne CIF on Monday while buyers quoted $810 a tonne, traders said.
Traders said sellers also asked for $825 a tonne CIF for November landing coconut oil, or a $15 premium above the buyers' bid of $810.
Coconut oil exports from the Philippines are expected to be limited for the rest of the week, traders said.

Philippine coconut exports fell by 40.9 percent to 1.064 million tonnes in the first nine months of the year from the year-ago level of 1.801 million tonnes, the trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines Inc (UCAP) said last week.
UCAP said the decline in exports from January to September was a result of an across-the-board drop in exports of coconut products.
Coconut oil exports for that period decreased by 41.9 percent from a year earlier, to 596,095 tonnes, UCAP said.
